description: PodVolumeStatus represents the status of an individual volume used by a pod.

healthStatus.description: VolumeHealthStatus contains health information for a volume reported by a CSI controller or node plugin.

healthConditions.description: healthConditions is the set of health conditions reported by a CSI plugin. At most 16 conditions may be reported. An empty list means the CSI driver either does not support volume health or has not reported it yet. If the driver supports volume health and the volume is healthy, a Healthy condition is reported.

items.description: VolumeHealthCondition represents a health condition reported for a volume. Both pod and PVC reuse this type to report volume health in their status fields.

message.description: message is a human-readable description. Maximum permitted length of a message is 1024 bytes.

reason.description: reason is a brief CamelCase machine-parseable reason. Together with status it forms the unique identity of a condition entry. Maximum permitted length of a reason is 256 bytes.

status.description:
status is the machine-parseable health category. Possible values are: - "Unknown": the driver reported an unknown health status, or a status Kubernetes does not recognize. The volume must not be considered healthy. - "Inaccessible": the volume cannot be accessed. - "DataLoss": data loss has been detected on the volume. - "Degraded": the volume is functioning with reduced capability. - "Healthy": the volume is healthy.

This field allows additional enum values to be added to VolumeHealthStatusType via CSI spec change. A future version of a CSI driver may emit health conditions that Kubernetes components are not aware of.

A writer which does not know how to handle incoming new VolumeHealthStatusType may classify the status as unknown.

A reader which does not know how to handle new VolumeHealthStatusType MUST only use it for health reporting purposes.

lastTransitionTime.description: Time is a wrapper around time.Time which supports correct marshaling to YAML and JSON.  Wrappers are provided for many of the factory methods that the time package offers.

name.description: name matches an entry in pod.spec.volumes.
